source_text: Before the access panel is removed, it should be made sure that hydraulic system B has been depressurized and that the reservoir gauge is reading 0 psi. The 8 screws holding the panel are then removed while the panel is being supported so that it does not fall.

Clean the filter bowl using an approved solvent and allow it to dry for at least 15 minutes, after which the new O-ring can be installed, making sure it isn't twisted, and the bowl is then torqued to 18 Nm.

The brake wear pin should be measured with the parking brake set; if the pin protrudes less than 1.5 mm from the housing, the brake assembly has to be replaced, otherwise the measurement is just recorded in the logbook.

After the new fuel boost pump has been installed, connect the electrical connector, energize the pump for not more than 30 seconds and check that the pressure indication rises to between 22 and 28 psi without any leakage being seen at the inlet flange.

The outflow valve, which is located on the aft pressure bulkhead, is driven by two independent electric motors, and it is used for regulating the rate at which cabin air is being discharged overboard so that cabin altitude stays below 8000 ft.

Each pitot probe contains a heating element rated at 115 V AC that keeps ice from forming on the probe tip; a current sensor in the probe heater controller monitors the element and will cause an amber caution light to come on if current falls below 0.5 A.

The emergency locator transmitter is powered by a lithium battery pack with a service life of 6 years, and when activated either manually or by its internal g-switch, it transmits on 121.5 MHz and 406 MHz simultaneously.

Located forward of the main spar, the rotor damper consists of an elastomeric bearing bonded between two steel plates and functions by absorbing lead-lag motion of the blade, so that ground resonance doesn't develop during start-up.

WARNING: Since the oxygen generators get extremely hot when they're activated, reaching temperatures of up to 260 °C, gloves need to be worn and the container should never be handled until it has been allowed to cool for 30 minutes.

CAUTION: Applying more than 45 Nm to the drain valve nut can result in the threads in the tank boss being stripped, so a calibrated torque wrench should always be used and the nut must not be reused if it is damaged.

WARNING: There is a risk of electrical shock from the de-ice brush block because 28 V DC may still be present even after the switch is selected off, therefore circuit breakers C12 and C14 must be opened and tagged before any work is started.
CAUTION: Make sure that no metal tools are left in the engine inlet after the inspection is finished, because foreign object damage to the fan blades could occur when the engine is next started.

If the smoke detector fault light stays on after the system test, the most likely cause is a dirty optical chamber, but a failed detector or a broken wire in harness W210 can also be the reason, so first the chamber should be cleaned and the test repeated before any components are replaced.

When the wiper motor runs but the blade doesn't move, check whether the drive shaft spline is worn; if it is not worn, the converter gearbox is probably faulty and has to be replaced, which takes approximately 2 hours.

An APU start that is aborted with an overtemperature message usually means that the EGT exceeded 980 °C during acceleration; inspect the fuel nozzle for coking and check the starter for low cranking speed, which should be at least 12 percent within 10 seconds.

Low pressure in the potable water system with the compressor running is normally caused by a leaking drain valve or a clogged inlet screen, and both should be checked in that order, a pressure below 20 psi being considered abnormal.
